title: Constitution article
description: ADR-0009. One registered article of a project's constitution, one article per file under the registry's 'articles/' directory, the file named by the article's id. The registry is the source: an article keeps its source span, exceptions and related articles, and only the obligations its 'enforced_by' entries name are covered, each entry naming the exact predicate it verifies, so a check that verifies part of an article never reads as verifying the article. Registries live in an overlay that a project record names (project 'constitution.registry'); this package holds only this shape and invented fixtures. An article is configuration, not a durable run artifact, so it carries a 'schema' marker and a version but not common's envelope.

schema_version.description: The version of this shape the article was written against. The overlay pins an agent-kit version, so a change here reaches it as a deliberate upgrade (ADR-0009 decision 1).

version.description: The article's own version. Raised whenever its normative text changes; every compiled rule, block reason and review finding cites the id and this version together.

theme.description: The article's theme, recorded here so classification is never read from an id prefix (ADR-0009 decision 2). An article that changes theme keeps its id.

tier.description: 'hard-constraint' holds only through a mechanism that does not depend on the agent or a hook running, and a coverage report fails one that no 'boundary' entry in 'enforced_by' covers (ADR-0009, design point 1). 'default' is followed unless an exception applies. 'judgment' asks for weighing rather than a rule.

source.description: Where the article's text comes from. The quote is the source's own words, never a paraphrase.

why.description: The reason the article exists. It stays with the article when a check lands, so the check is never the only record of why.

do.description: Obligations to do something. Each one is an obligation coverage counts separately.

dont.description: Obligations not to do something. Each one is an obligation coverage counts separately.

exceptions.description: The cases the source itself carves out. An exception the source does not state is a proposed amendment, not an entry here.

enforced_by.description: What covers which obligation. An absent or empty list means nothing covers the article, which a coverage report lists rather than hides.

review_questions.description: Questions a reviewer asks of a change that triggers the article. Each is answerable from the change and its records.

translation_fixtures.description: Inputs a compiled form of the article must judge the way the article does: a check, a path rule or a review question translated from it.

article_id.description: Immutable once assigned and never reused. Both shapes are admitted so the choice stays the overlay's: a themed prefix and a number ('SAFE-003'), or a plain number ('12').

document.description: The source document, as a path relative to the registry root.

section.description: The section heading the quote sits under, as the document spells it.

id.description: Unique within the article; 'enforced_by' entries name it.

permits.description: What the exception allows that the article otherwise forbids or requires.

requires.description: What must be on record for the exception to apply, such as an approved decision. An exception that requires nothing applies whenever its condition holds.

conflicts.description: Articles this one can collide with on the same change.

tie_breakers.description: How a collision resolves. Each entry says this article prevails over another, and when.

when.description: The condition under which this article prevails. Absent: whenever the two collide.

triggers.description: What makes a change subject to the article. A cross-cutting article applies to every change; any other names at least one trigger.

enforcement.description: One mechanism covering one obligation. 'boundary' holds without the agent or a hook running: a sandbox, a scoped credential, branch protection, a required check on the protected branch. 'check' is a deterministic check run where the agent can also run it. 'guard' is the opt-in guard runtime, early feedback and never the boundary. 'review' is a review seat or a required human review. A passing mechanism is evidence for its predicate alone.

mechanism.description: The specific mechanism, named so it can be found: a check id, a ruleset, a hook rule id.

covers.description: The id of the 'do' or 'dont' obligation this entry covers.

predicate.description: The exact predicate the mechanism verifies, which may be narrower than the obligation it covers.

covers.description: The obligation the fixture exercises, when it exercises one.

path.description: Where the content would live, so path triggers apply to it.
